signature.name: Table Mountain Aerial Cableway
signature.detail: The cable car up Table Mountain is Cape Town's defining experience, with rotating cars and sweeping views over the city and both oceans. Go early in the morning to beat the crowds and wind, and check the weather before you buy tickets since the cableway closes in high winds.

signature.name: V&A Waterfront
signature.detail: This working harbor is the city's liveliest gathering place, packed with restaurants, shops and views of Table Mountain across the water. It is an easy walk from the city center or a short taxi ride, and evenings are best for dinner with the mountain lit up behind you.

signature.name: Robben Island Prison
signature.detail: The ferry to Robben Island and the guided tour of Nelson Mandela's former prison cell is a sobering must-do for understanding South Africa's history. Book tickets well in advance, especially in summer, as ferries sell out and crossings depend on calm seas.

signature.name: Boulders Beach
signature.detail: A sheltered cove where you can watch African penguins up close from boardwalks and sometimes share the sand with them. Go early or late to avoid the midday crowds, and bring a windbreaker since the Cape wind can be strong.

signature.name: Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
signature.detail: This vast garden at the foot of Table Mountain showcases South Africa's unique flora, with a famous treetop walkway and seasonal blooms. Allow at least half a day, wear comfortable shoes, and consider a picnic on the lawns.

signature.name: Bo-Kaap
signature.detail: The brightly painted houses of this historic Cape Malay quarter make it one of the city's most photographed neighborhoods. Walk the steep streets respectfully since people live here, and stop for a koeksister or bobotie at a local cafe.

transport: Ride-hailing apps $2-5 for short trips; car rental $30-50 a day
